caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 120 of 1992.
lawyer:
Md. Amir Hossain, Advocate—For the Appellants. 
Syed Mahmood Hossain, Advocate—For the Respondents.
parties:
Roushan Rahman and others  ----- Appellants
Vs.
Abdul Hakim Majumder and ors  ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Gholam Rabbani J: This appeal is directed against the preliminary decree passed in a partition suit. Total area of the suit plot bearing No. 52/2 is 1.75 acre. Admittedly the predecessor in interest of the plaintiffs Md Faiz purchased 0.8 acre of land of the said plot by a registered sale deed dated 12-5-38 and the predecessor in interest of the defendants Yakub Ali purchased 0.52 acre of land of the said plot by a registered sale deed dated 19-5-38. In this suit plaintiffs sought partition of the suit land which is 0.60 acre out of the entire suit plot and which was purchased by Md. Faiz and Yeakub Ali who were two full brothers. 

 2. By the judgment and decree dated 26-11-91 learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit for partition in preliminary form to the effect that the plaintiffs will get a saham of 08 acres of land and defendants will get a saham for remaining .52 acres of land out of the suit land. 

 4. Mr. Md. Amir Hossain, learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the learned subordinate Judge should not have decreed the suit and the suit was not maintainable in view of fact that the entire area of the suit plot was not brought to hotch-potch. Learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs are possessing 0.8 acres of land as claimant by them with definite boundaries to the extreme west of the suit plot and that the defendants are possessing 0.52 acres of land with specific boundaries contiguous east to the land possessed by the plaintiffs. 

 5. Mr. Syed Mahmood Hossain, learned Advocate for the respondents, submits that even accepting the factual position as submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants it cannot be said that the plaintiffs are not entitled to a decree for partition as there is nothing on record to show that the suit land was partitioned among the parties by metes and bounds. 

 6. We have perused the record of the partition suit. It is well settled that a decree for partition is an equitable relief and, as such, a person seeking partition cannot be denied such relief on technical ground. In this suit we find that there is no technical flaw in granting the relief to the plaintiff as prayed for. However, in view of the materials available on record we find that the order portion of the judgment under appeal is required to be modified.
